info.title: Snipe-IT API (baton-snipe-it connector surface)
info.description:
Describes only the Snipe-IT endpoints baton-snipe-it calls. Scope is derived from pkg/snipe-it/client.go, users.go, and groups.go; response shapes are derived from the structs in those files and settled against Snipe-IT's own source, which is the authoritative reference for a self-hosted open-source application — app/Http/Transformers/UsersTransformer.php, GroupsTransformer.php, DatatablesTransformer.php, app/Http/Controllers/Api/GroupsController.php, and app/Http/Middleware/SetPaginationDefaults.php on the master branch (accessed 2026-09-23), cross-checked against snipe-it.readme.io.

Only the properties the connector's structs declare are modelled. Snipe-IT's user transformer alone returns roughly fifty; the omissions are deliberate — spec scope is connector scope.

Server: the instance's own base URL, supplied by config. The connector appends `api/v1` to it, and self-heals if the operator already included that suffix — see the note on validateCredentials.

Auth: a Snipe-IT personal API token sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.

Pagination: `limit`/`offset` on the users listing, with the connector pinning `limit` at 50 and stopping when a page comes back short. The groups listing is called with neither parameter — see the note on that operation.

servers.description: The Snipe-IT instance, from the connector's base-URL config. `api/v1` is appended by the client.

baseUrl.description: Instance base URL, without the api/v1 suffix.

tags.name: users
tags.description: Users, their group memberships, and their permission maps.

get.description:
The workhorse of this connector. It backs user resources (pkg/connector/user.go:83), group membership grants (pkg/connector/group.go:79, filtered by `group_id`), and both the entitlements and the grants derived from per-user permission maps (pkg/connector/role.go:96 and :254).

It is also the credential-validation probe, called with `limit=1` (pkg/snipe-it/client.go:31).

`limit` and `offset` are always sent, `limit` pinned at 50. The connector never reads the `total` it gets back — it stops when a page returns fewer rows than it asked for. That is correct for a stable collection but will end the walk early if a user is deleted mid-sync.

`group_id` is sent only when listing a group's members, and it is what makes group membership discoverable at all: there is no list-members-of-group route in this surface.

Snipe-IT accepts many more filters here — `search`, `sort`, `order`, `deleted`, `all`, `company_id`, `location_id`, and others. The connector sends none of them, so it syncs with Snipe-IT's defaults: active users only, ordered by `created_at desc`.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: Restrict the listing to members of one group. Sent only when enumerating a group's members; this is the connector's only route to group membership.

get.description:
Called only as the read half of the read-modify-write that group provisioning requires (pkg/snipe-it/groups.go:68 and :106). Snipe-IT has no add-member or remove-member route; the only way to change membership is to PATCH the user's whole group list, so the current list has to be fetched first.

This makes both provisioning operations non-atomic: a concurrent membership change between the GET and the PATCH is silently overwritten.

Unlike the listing, this returns a bare user object — no `total`/`rows` envelope.

patch.description:
Backs both granting and revoking group membership (pkg/snipe-it/groups.go:68 and :106). The body carries `groups` and nothing else — a full replacement of the user's group list, computed client-side from the getUser response:

- **Grant** sends the requested group ID followed by every group the user already had. If the user was already a member, the ID appears twice in the array; Snipe-IT's sync of the pivot table makes that harmless, but the connector does not check membership first.
- **Revoke** sends every existing group except the one being removed. Removing a user's last group sends an empty array, which `omitempty` on the struct tag then drops from the JSON entirely — so the request body serialises to `{}` and Snipe-IT has no `groups` key to act on. The revoke silently does nothing in that case.

Snipe-IT's PATCH accepts many other user fields; the connector sends only `groups`.

The response is not decoded.

200.description: User updated. Body not decoded by the connector.

403.description: The token's user lacks permission to edit this user.

get.description:
Source of the connector's group resources (pkg/connector/group.go:124) and of the entitlements and grants derived from per-group permission maps (pkg/connector/role.go:78 and :219).

**This route is paginated, and the connector sends no pagination parameters.** `GroupsController::index` reads `app('api_limit_value')`, which `SetPaginationDefaults` sets to `config('app.max_results')` — the instance's `MAX_RESULTS`, default 500 — whenever no `limit` is supplied. A request with no `limit` therefore returns at most that many groups, not all of them. The connector decodes the `total` the response carries but never compares it against the number of rows, and the comment at role.go:77 records the opposite belief: "Groups doesn't have pagination." An instance with more groups than its `MAX_RESULTS` silently syncs only the first page.

The route also requires the token's user to be a **superadmin**: `GroupsController::index` calls `authorize('superadmin')` before anything else. A token belonging to a non-superadmin gets a 403 here even if it can read users perfectly well.

Snipe-IT's transformer returns `users_count`, `notes`, `created_by`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` alongside the three properties the connector decodes.

One quirk of the client is worth recording: on HTTP 429 it returns the partially-decoded response and a nil error rather than propagating the rate-limit failure, so a throttled groups call reads as an empty group list rather than an error.

200.description: A page of groups — capped at the instance's MAX_RESULTS because no limit is sent.

403.description: The token's user is not a superadmin.

429.description: Rate limited. The client swallows this and returns an empty group list with no error.

bearerAuth.description: Snipe-IT personal API token, attached by uhttp.NewBearerAuth.

UserId.name: id
UserId.description: Numeric user ID — `User.id`, which is also the connector's user resource ID.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Rows per page. The connector pins this at 50 for syncs and 1 for the validation probe. When omitted, Snipe-IT substitutes the instance's MAX_RESULTS (default 500); a requested value above MAX_RESULTS is ignored in favour of MAX_RESULTS.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Rows to skip. Always sent, starting at 0 and advancing by 50.

UsersResponse.description: Snipe-IT's shared list envelope. It also carries `current_page`, `per_page`, `total_pages`, `prev_page_url`, and `next_page_url`; the connector decodes none of them and paginates by offset arithmetic instead.

total.description: Total matching users. Decoded but never read — the walk terminates on a short page instead.

GroupsResponse.description: The same list envelope for groups. Also used as the shape of a user's nested `groups` object, which carries the same `total`/`rows` pair but whose rows hold only `id` and `name`.

total.description: Total groups on the instance. Decoded but never compared against the number of rows returned, which is what hides the truncation described on listGroups.

User.description: A Snipe-IT user. Snipe-IT's transformer returns roughly fifty properties; only the ten the connector declares are listed here.

id.description: Numeric ID. The connector's user resource ID and the path parameter for the provisioning read-modify-write — parity-critical.

email.description: Email address. Snipe-IT permits users without one.

employee_num.description: Employee number. Null upstream when unset, which decodes to the empty string here.

activated.description: Whether the account is active. Drives the user's enabled/disabled status.

groups.description: The user's groups, in the same total/rows envelope. Snipe-IT emits **null** rather than an empty envelope when the user has no groups, which decodes into the zero-valued struct. The nested rows carry only `id` and `name` — no `permissions` — so the Permissions map on a nested group is always empty.

permissions.description: The user's own permission map, distinct from any inherited through groups. Drives role entitlements and grants — parity-critical.

Group.description: A Snipe-IT group. Snipe-IT also returns `users_count`, `notes`, `created_by`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`.

id.description: Numeric ID. The connector's group resource ID and the `group_id` filter value — parity-critical.

permissions.description: The group's permission map. Drives role entitlements and expandable grants — parity-critical. Populated on the groups listing; always empty on the copy nested inside a user.

Permissions.description:
Snipe-IT's permission map: permission name to tri-state value. Snipe-IT stores this as a JSON blob on the row and `decodePermissions()` casts each value to an integer before returning it — but older rows and some code paths emit the values as strings. The connector's custom unmarshaller accepts either, decoding to a string in both cases, which is why the values below are typed as strings rather than integers.

Keys are not a fixed set: they are whatever permission slugs the instance's version defines, plus the role-shaped keys (`superuser`, `admin`, `user`, `import`, `other`) the connector treats specially.

additionalProperties.description: Tri-state permission value. `1` granted, `-1` denied, `0` inherited. Only `1` produces a grant; `0` and `-1` are both skipped.

PatchUserBody.description: Body of updateUserGroups. `groups` carries `omitempty`, so an empty array is dropped from the JSON entirely and the request body serialises to `{}` — see the note on the operation.

groups.description: The user's complete new group list, computed client-side. Not a delta — whatever is sent replaces the existing memberships.
